meta.what: (19) Payments to Rosatom for nuclear plants abroad and for nuclear fuel; (26) interest and principal paid to Russia on Russian state (and state-bank) loans, with drawdowns shown separately. Per country (payer), 2019-2026.
meta.units: EUR bn nominal per year; 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. USD converted at ECB yearly averages 2019 1.1195, 2020 1.1422, 2021 1.183, 2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.16. Ranges ~90%.
meta.method: Money to Russia = (a) payments to Rosatom from the buyer's OWN funds that are not already in customs or services data (rosatom.to_add) + (b) a negative correction where customs imports from Russia were paid with Russian money (Russian loan or Rosatom's own capital) but trade_full counts them as the buyer's payments (rosatom.customs_correction) + (c) principal and interest actually transferred to Russia (state_loans.repayments_to_russia). Loan-financed Rosatom work is Russian money paying a Russian company: it is not counted, and the matching drawdowns must NOT be subtracted again. Drawdowns of budget/refinancing loans (Belarus) are real money from Russia to the borrower; net them only if the map wants net flows. Pre-war level = mean 2019-2021. World Bank International Debt Statistics (IDS, creditor = Russian Federation, PPG bilateral + commercial banks) are actuals to 2024 and contractual projections for 2025+.

rosatom.customs_correction_how: Türkiye's HS 73+84+85 imports from Russia (Comtrade) minus ~0.05 non-nuclear base: 0.02 (2019) → 0.97 EUR bn (2024). overlaps: 1) Fuel and enrichment (HS 2844 enriched uranium, HS 8401 fuel assemblies/reactor parts) are goods and already inside trade_full imports_from_RUS (US 0.5-1.1, China 0.1-1.5, Korea 0.2-0.6, France up to 0.4, Czechia/Slovakia/Hungary/Finland VVER fuel 0.03-0.3 EUR bn/yr). Nothing is added for fuel. Their price rise is already in prices.json's uranium index. 2) Construction services: Eurostat/BaTiS services imports from Russia (uncovered.json) for Egypt (0.2), Bangladesh (0.03-0.19), Hungary (0.08-0.18) are far below Rosatom's work, so rosatom.to_add does not double count in the central case; low ends allow for partial overlap. Finland's Hanhikivi payments are already in its services fall. 3) Loan-financed equipment in customs: Bangladesh is already halved by nonreport.json paid_share 0.5 (no further correction); Egypt and India get a negative customs_correction; Türkiye's Akkuyu equipment (Rosatom's own money) gets a negative customs_correction. 4) (19) vs (26): Rosatom work financed by a Russian state loan is NOT in rosatom.to_add (only the buyer's own share). The loan is counted when it is repaid (state_loans principal/interest). So add (19) to_add + (26) repayments and do not subtract drawdowns of project loans (EGY, BGD, HUN, IND, Belarus Ostrovets part). 5) nonreport.json treats (1 - paid_share) of Russian supplies as Russian credit/support to the partner (BGD, CUB, SYR...). Do not also book state_loans drawdowns for those as Russian support, or it is counted twice. 6) Military credits (Indonesia, Azerbaijan, Viet Nam, India) are inside the IDS lines; the related arms imports are not part of the map's trade (arms are excluded), so no overlap. 7) Belarus: other.json/round4b count Belarus's military support to Russia; loan service here is a separate money flow. Belarus drawdowns since 2022 are mainly refinancing, i.e. Russia lending Minsk the money to pay Russia: the honest number for Belarus is the NET flow.
notes: IDS 2025-2026 values are contractual projections on debt outstanding at end-2024, not actuals; overridden where news shows deferrals or arrears.

Bangladesh 2022-2024: IDS records interest due, but money stayed in a Bangladesh Bank escrow account; the series counts only money reaching Russia. If the escrow (~USD 0.8-1.0bn) was released in late 2025/2026, it lands in those years (central 0.5 + 0.4 USD bn).

Hungary is an educated guess (D): no ÁKK drawdown/prepayment series for 2022-2026 found. US sanctions on Gazprombank (Nov 2024) disrupted payments; the US lifted Paks-related restrictions in mid-2025.
Türkiye: Akkuyu is build-own-operate. Russia sent Rosatom capital into Türkiye (several USD bn in 2022) - money from Russia, not to it; not counted here.

Arrears and stops (Viet Nam, Iraq, Bangladesh 2022-24) lower the change vs 2019-2021 and so read as toward Ukraine, although they were caused by sanctions on payment channels, not by the borrower's choice; the sanctions label could mark them.

Repayments on loans contracted before 2022 follow a schedule set before the war. A rise in scheduled payments (Egypt, Bangladesh, India as drawdowns accumulate) is not a war-time choice; the builder may prefer to treat the contractual schedule as the no-war counterfactual for (26), so that only deviations count.
